source: Event types follow real mission experience: solar particle events upsetting flight computers, Deep Space Network scheduling conflicts, lunar lander navigation losses in engine-blown dust, wheel and drill actuator faults on Mars rovers, programme budget reductions. Probabilities and magnitudes are game balance values.
units: probability is the chance the event happens once in its phase; rate_per_day is used instead for events that can strike at any time in a phase. Effects: lose_days (days of operations lost), lose_data_fraction (share of stored data lost), power_loss_fraction (share of generated power lost for the rest of the mission), budget_cut_fraction (share of the budget cap removed), slip_lunar_months (landing date moves by whole lunar months), disable_slot (the part in that slot stops working), mission_loss. A mitigation applies when its condition is true for the design: it multiplies the probability and the magnitude. drag_factor multiplies atmospheric drag on an orbiter for the rest of the mission.

events.name: Budget cut
events.description: Congress trims the programme's budget before launch.
events.unmitigated_why: The budget cap fell by 8 %. With little reserve left, the overrun forced a descope.

mitigations.why: You kept at least 10 % of the budget unspent, so the cut came out of the margin and nothing had to be removed.

events.name: Late hardware
events.description: A part that had never flown is not ready in time.
events.unmitigated_why: Low-readiness hardware arrived late. The landing slipped by a lunar month and the lighting you planned for moved on without you.

events.name: Solar particle event
events.description: A solar flare sprays the spacecraft with energetic protons.
events.unmitigated_why: The commercial-grade computer crashed in the radiation and spent four days in safe mode while controllers rebuilt its memory.

mitigations.why: The radiation-hardened computer rode out the storm without a reset.
The backup computer took over within hours while the primary recovered.

events.name: Dust blackout on final descent
events.description: The engine plume throws up a curtain of dust in the last thirty metres.
events.unmitigated_why: The altimeter lost the ground in the dust and the lander came down blind, doubling the chance of a bad touchdown.

mitigations.why: The hazard lidar had already mapped the touchdown spot before the dust rose, and the lander flew the last metres on inertial guidance.
Terrain-relative navigation had fixed the lander's position before the dust rose, so only the last seconds were blind.

events.name: Wheel actuator fault
events.description: Abrasive dust works its way into a drive motor.
events.unmitigated_why: A drive motor seized and the rover could not move again. Everything it had not yet reached stayed out of reach.

mitigations.why: The redundant drive train carried on with the failed motor freewheeling.
Sealed, independently driven wheels halve the chance of a seized motor.

events.name: Drill jam
events.description: The bit binds in ground as hard as concrete.
events.unmitigated_why: The drill jammed. Freeing it by commands from Earth, one careful step at a time, took three days.

mitigations.why: The onboard computer sensed the torque rising and backed the bit out by itself before it stuck fast.

events.name: Deep Space Network conflict
events.description: Another mission declares an emergency and takes your antenna time.
events.unmitigated_why: Your passes were handed to a spacecraft in trouble, and new data overwrote 15 % of what was waiting to be sent.

mitigations.why: Your data goes through the commercial relay, which the Deep Space Network schedule does not touch.
Relay passes are booked on the orbiters months ahead, so an emergency elsewhere rarely touches them.
The large recorder held everything until the next pass.

events.name: Colder than predicted
events.description: The shadowed ground turns out colder than the orbital maps said.
events.unmitigated_why: Heaters ran 35 % harder than planned in shadow, draining the battery faster on every sortie and every night.

mitigations.why: The radioisotope heaters do not care how cold it is outside.
The generator's waste heat kept the vehicle warm without drawing on the battery.

events.name: Dust on the solar arrays
events.description: Electrostatically charged dust kicked up by the wheels clings to the panels.
events.unmitigated_why: Dust cut solar power by 12 % for the rest of the mission.

mitigations.why: A radioisotope generator has no panels for dust to cover.
The mast holds the array high above the dust the wheels throw up.

events.name: Regional dust storm
events.description: A dust storm the size of a continent dims the Sun for weeks and leaves a coat of dust behind.
events.unmitigated_why: The storm and the dust it left on the panels cut solar power by 35 % for the rest of the mission. Opportunity was lost to a storm like this in 2018.

mitigations.why: A radioisotope generator does not care how dark the sky gets: Curiosity worked straight through the 2018 global storm.
The tilting mast shook most of the dust off its array once the storm had passed.

events.name: Thin air on entry day
events.description: Dust in the atmosphere has warmed and thinned it since the forecast was made.
events.unmitigated_why: The parachute opened lower and faster than planned, leaving seconds less to find a safe spot: the chance of a bad touchdown nearly doubled.

mitigations.why: The hazard lidar needs only a few seconds to pick a clear spot, and it had them.
Terrain-relative navigation knew where the lander was the moment the heat shield dropped, and steered to its pre-mapped safe zone with the time it had.

events.name: Reaction wheel fault
events.description: A wheel bearing starts to drag and the wheel is switched off.
events.unmitigated_why: With a wheel gone the satellite could no longer hold still on a target. Every image after that day was smeared and useless.

mitigations.why: The spare wheel spun up and pointing carried on as before.
Magnetic torquers have no moving parts to wear out.

events.name: Ground station outage
events.description: A storm takes the ground station off the air for two days.
events.unmitigated_why: With nowhere to send it, new images overwrote 30 % of what was waiting in the recorder.

mitigations.why: The large recorder held two days of images until the station came back.

events.name: Active Sun
events.description: The Sun turns out more active than forecast and the upper atmosphere swells.
events.unmitigated_why: The air at orbital height became three times denser, and drag pulled the orbit down three times faster than planned. In 2022 a batch of 38 new satellites was lost this way.

mitigations.why: The thruster simply burned a little more often to hold the orbit.
The electric thruster made up the extra drag with propellant to spare.
